premiseSetup.question: What does a $500,000 house actually cost over 30 years?
premiseSetup.audienceStakes: Buyers comparing a sticker price with the full cash outflow of owning the same home.
premiseSetup.openingPromise: The sticker price is only the beginning; the video separates the purchase price from recurring owner costs.

premisePayoff.payoffStatement: A scenario-calculated lifetime cash outflow, shown as the sum of the declared purchase, financing, tax, insurance and maintenance assumptions.
premisePayoff.limitation: No rent model, lending-rate series, property-tax growth series or maintenance series is sourced for this scenario, so the total is a scenario calculation and not a market measurement.

hypotheses.title: The Real 30-Year Cost of a $500,000 House
hypotheses.thumbnailConcept: A single house diagram with the $500,000 sticker price beside a second meter that grows from the declared cost categories.
hypotheses.openingVisual: The price tag appears first, then a lifetime-cost meter grows from the declared purchase, financing, tax, insurance and maintenance assumptions.

hypotheses.title: Rent vs Buy: The Costs Everyone Forgets
hypotheses.thumbnailConcept: The same home split between a buy path and a rent path under the declared assumptions.
hypotheses.openingVisual: Two cumulative-cost paths appear side by side, with the rental side labelled as a declared scenario input rather than a sourced model.

hypotheses.title: Why a $500,000 House Can Cost So Much More
hypotheses.thumbnailConcept: A cutaway house exposing financing, tax, insurance and maintenance cost layers around the purchase price.
hypotheses.openingVisual: Roof, foundation, loan and insurance layers separate into a cost waterfall built from the declared scenario assumptions.
